title: codemother answers inspect over the bus
intention: CodeMother answers an `inspect` verb over the bus: a request naming one of build_inspector's public judges and its arguments gets back exactly the findings list a direct call returns.
why: Child of 4c4addb09adb (CairnCommons/tickets/4c4addb09adb-the-code-pipeline-s-inspectors-and-gates-live-inside-codemother.json). Akien 2026-10-27, open-0b203e62c1e0: 'everything that has no purpose other than helping our design and build pipeline for code belongs to code mother.' Outline 9.4.3.3.4, Akien 2026-11-13 on Q#88: once build_inspector moves into CodeMother, code outside her reaches it over the bus — the 18 crossing calls in transitions.py, the other code sites and the proofs that run a sieve over themselves; no published client tool, no fifth exception: 'over the bus. that's what it's for?'
traces_to: outline 9.4.3.3.4 and 10.3.5; RULE 1 (encapsulation, 17.13.1); Law 6 (one owner gates writes)
how: D1: VERB. codemother's device declares `inspect`; body {'judge': <name>, 'args': [...], 'kwargs': {...}}. The judges it answers are an allow-list in the shim, exactly the names outside code calls today (measured 2026-11-13: the 18 crossing calls in transitions.py — crossing_emission, crossing_rules, crossing_named_ticket, crossing_fixme, crossing_demo, crossing_clearance, crossing_proof_named, working_tree_clean, buildme_rides_the_chart/_intent/_sorted/_outline_check, buildme_has_no_open_questions, proved_answers_the_chart, crossing_durability, inspect, crossing_quorum, reason_has_referent — plus resolves_to, list_runs and the sieves the proofs run over themselves). A name off the list is refused, naming it (Law 7). The reply's data is the findings list, unchanged. D2: WIRE SHAPE. Non-JSON arguments cross as their standing serial form and are rebuilt on codemother's side: a Path as its string; a Workflow as render(wf, target) and parse_workflow on arrival; a ticket object as its id. One helper beside the verb owns both directions so caller and answerer cannot disagree. D3: PROOF, one tooth per clause, over the scratch bus (cairn/devices/cairn/tools/scratch_bus).

decisions.text: D1: VERB. codemother's device declares `inspect`; body {'judge': <name>, 'args': [...], 'kwargs': {...}}. The judges it answers are an allow-list in the shim, exactly the names outside code calls today (measured 2026-11-13: the 18 crossing calls in transitions.py — crossing_emission, crossing_rules, crossing_named_ticket, crossing_fixme, crossing_demo, crossing_clearance, crossing_proof_named, working_tree_clean, buildme_rides_the_chart/_intent/_sorted/_outline_check, buildme_has_no_open_questions, proved_answers_the_chart, crossing_durability, inspect, crossing_quorum, reason_has_referent — plus resolves_to, list_runs and the sieves the proofs run over themselves). A name off the list is refused, naming it (Law 7). The reply's data is the findings list, unchanged.

D2: WIRE SHAPE. Non-JSON arguments cross as their standing serial form and are rebuilt on codemother's side: a Path as its string; a Workflow as render(wf, target) and parse_workflow on arrival; a ticket object as its id. One helper owns both directions so caller and answerer cannot disagree. It is a tool codemother publishes, cairn/devices/codemother/tools/inspect_wire/ (published_by_device true), because the callers (17d570c10390, 149b9a1ab9c4) sit outside codemother and RULE 1 lets them reach into her only through a published tool. A Workflow crosses as _render_at(wf, wf.cursor, wf.phase), the one string assembler render() also goes through: render(wf, target) moves the cursor and stamps 'waiting', and clause 3 asks for the caller's Workflow rebuilt equal.
D3: PROOF, one tooth per clause, over the scratch bus (cairn/devices/cairn/tools/scratch_bus).
